h201.text: This is Momo. This is a teddy bear. Two eyes. Soft fur. One is living. One is not.

h202.text: Easy? Then try the six things in our box.

h203.text: First, a practice round. The teddy bear. Point left for living. Point right for non-living. Go!

m207.text: But it has eyes and fur like me. Why isn't it living?

h208.text: The teddy bear is a non-living thing. Eyes and fur are only how it looks. We need better clues.

h301.text: Here is the game. It's You against the Buddies. You lock in first. Then Pip, Basil and Momo answer.

h302.text: Every time you are right, put up one finger on your other hand. Five fingers wins. No lock-in, no point. And a cicak is hiding in this video. Find it!

h303.text: Today you will learn what diversity means, how to classify things into groups, and how to tell living things from non-living things.

h401.text: Our six things came from here. A void deck and a garden in Toa Payoh. Look around.

h402.text: A mynah. Ants. A papaya tree. A bench. A bicycle. A blue recycling bin. So many different things!

h403.text: There is a great variety of living and non-living things around us. This is called diversity.

b404.text: So many! How do we keep track?

h405.text: We put them into groups. Let's start with six.

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

h502.text: Day one. Six things, one box. The lid has holes, so air can get in. The mealworm has oats to eat and a juicy carrot for water. The plant gets water, and light from the window.

h601.text: Round one. The wind-up robot. Look at it go! Point left for living. Point right for non-living.

b603.text: Living! It moves, so it's living!

p604.text: Non-living. I saw you wind it up, Basil.

m605.text: Non-living. Does it ever get hungry?

h606.text: Watch. The robot stops. A spring inside was pushing it.

h606b.text: Nobody winds it up, so it stays still. All night. All of day two.

h607.text: It does not need water, food or air. It does not grow. The wind-up robot is a non-living thing.

b609.text: Aww. So moving is not the clue!

m610.text: Then is a thing that stays still always non-living?

h701.text: Round two. Day two. The green bean. It is a seed. It has not moved at all. Living, or non-living? Point!

p703.text: Non-living. I watched it for one whole day. It did nothing.

m704.text: Living! It's green, like a leaf.

b705.text: Living! Taugeh grows from green beans. I eat taugeh!

h706.text: Three buddies, two answers. Let's shrink down and watch. Quietly.

h707.text: You are tiny now. The green bean is as big as a bus.

h709.text: The skin splits. A root pushes out.

h710.text: Nobody wound it up. Nobody pushed it. It is growing by itself.

h711.text: The green bean is a living thing. It was living all along. It took in water. Then it began to grow.

p713.text: I was careful. But I did not watch long enough.

h714.text: Momo, living is right. But green is only how it looks. A green pencil is non-living.

m715.text: No point for me! So what ARE the clues?

h801.text: Not how it looks. Not whether it moves. Ask two things. What does it need? What can it do?

h802.text: Living things need water, food and air. Living things grow, respond to changes and reproduce. You will test these in the next two episodes.

c803.text: Does it move? That's NOT the clue! What does it NEED? What can it DO?

h901.text: Day ten. Time to sort all six into two groups: living things and non-living things. Momo, you go first.

h903.text: Something is not right. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

h904.text: Arms crossed? One finger up! Look. The teddy bear is sitting with the mealworm. Momo sorted by soft and hard.

m905.text: I wanted to know how they feel! Good sort. Wrong question.

h906.text: Momo did put things into groups. Alike things together. Different things apart.

h907.text: Classification is the grouping of things based on their similarities and differences.

h908.text: You can choose soft or hard. But our question is living or non-living. So we use the real clues. Has anyone done that?

p1001.text: My homework from Day one. I fixed the green bean after Round two.

h1002.text: Showdown! Double points. Pip made a table with two columns. One thing is still in the wrong column.

h1003.text: Is it one, the wind-up robot? Two, the plant? Or three, the pebble? Show me with your fingers.

b1005.text: Two! We water that plant. It needs water.

m1006.text: Two! I saw a new leaf.

p1007.text: But it never moved out of its pot!

h1008.text: Watch the plant, from day one to day fourteen. It stays in its pot. But it has a new leaf. And it grows towards the light from the window. The plant is a living thing.

p1009.text: Fixed! A plant stays in one place. But it is a living thing.

h1010.text: Two fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

h1101.text: Pip used a table. The same two groups can be shown in other ways too.

h1102.text: We can present our classification using pictures, a table, and a graphic organiser.

h1201.text: Day thirty. What is under the cloth?

h1202.text: The green bean is a tall plant now. The mealworm is bigger. The plant has new leaves. And the teddy bear, the robot and the pebble? Exactly the same.

h1203.text: Three living things. Three non-living things.

c1204.text: Does it move? That's NOT the clue! What does it NEED? What can it DO?

h1301.text: Show me your score hand! More than three? You beat the Buddies. Five fingers? High five!

h1302.text: Did you spot the cicak? It was on the window frame on day fourteen. Is a cicak living or non-living? Tell someone at home.

h1304.text: A drooping plant isn't sad. What does it need? Lock in your answer for next time.
